# GoogleG asset

Google's full-colour "G", 20×20pt with a **transparent** background, at
@1x/@2x/@3x. Shared by `WelcomeView` (iOS) and `MacWelcomeView` (Mac).

## Provenance — this is Google's artwork, not a redraw

Generated by `scripts/extract-google-g-logo.py` from the official
`signin-assets.zip` linked off
<https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines>.

Google ships that pack as *finished buttons*: the G is already composited onto
one of the three approved fills (Light `#FFFFFF`, Dark `#131314`, Neutral
`#F2F2F2`). There is no bare transparent G in it. The script recovers the matte
algebraically from two renders over two known fills — it never keys or repaints
a pixel — and then checks itself by re-compositing onto the Neutral fill it
deliberately held out of the solve. Agreement is within 8-bit rounding
(≤1.71/255), so what ships here *is* Google's logo with the fill separated out.

Re-run after any refresh of Google's pack:

```
curl -sSLO https://developers.google.com/static/identity/images/signin-assets.zip
unzip -q signin-assets.zip -d /tmp/g && \
  python3 scripts/extract-google-g-logo.py /tmp/g \
    apps/pendingbot/Resources/Assets.xcassets/GoogleG.imageset/
```

## One asset, not a light/dark pair

The asset catalog can carry `appearances` variants, and it's tempting to ship
two. Don't: Google's light and dark buttons draw the **identical** G — same
path, same gradient — and only the fill underneath changes. A dark-mode variant
would by definition be a *modified* Google logo, which the guidelines forbid.
The theming belongs to the button, not the mark.

## Rules that constrain this asset

- Standard full-colour G only. Never recolour, add a stroke, tint it as a
  template, or drop it into a `Circle().fill()`.
- It must sit on one of the three approved fills — see `Theme.Palette.googlePill`
  / `googlePillStroke`, which carry the guideline's exact hexes.
- Keep at least the guideline's clear space around it (Google's own 44pt button
  gives a 20pt G 12pt of padding on every side).
- <https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines>

## History

Until 2026-08-23 this imageset held a single 80×80 `g-logo.png` in **RGB with
no alpha channel** — the white button fill was baked into the pixels, so dark
mode showed a white square around the G (human todo #8) — and only the 1x slot
was filled, so retina screens upscaled it. Both are fixed here.
